outcome: evidence of sphincter disruption on translabial ultrasound
cohort: The study included 146 women who were diagnosed with obstetric anal sphincter injuries between 2005 and 2015 and attended an invitation for follow-up.
finding: Symptoms of anal incontinence were highly prevalent (51%) with a high bother score, and St Mark scores were associated with residual internal anal sphincter defects and levator avulsion, with higher tear grades leading to more defects and lower manometry pressures.
cross-section timing: At a mean follow-up of 6.6 years (range 1.7-11.9 years) after delivery
